Samantha — thanks, this is helpful. Quick clarifying questions so we can size conservatively for the pilot:

- Burst shape: is the 2.5x peak applied uniformly across the hour or concentrated into <10 minute microbursts? Your CSV looks like a few short high-concurrency spikes but want to confirm.
- Session shape: are sessions typically 3–6 messages (interactive) or longer flows (10+ messages)?
- Prompt/response tokens: can you give average and 95th percentile for prompt tokens and response tokens? If you don’t have p95, ballpark numbers are fine.
- Latency SLO: you mentioned p95 token latency 250–350 ms — is that for end-to-end response completion or per-token generation latency? We size differently based on either.

I'll loop in Marissa for kernel/quantization guidance and Karthik for session affinity advice. If you want an initial conservative thumbprint we can provide a quick napkin estimate, then run a short pilot with 24–48 hours of traffic replay to validate.

I attached a short intake checklist to this reply (see referenced attachments).

—Marcus

Forwarding quick technical notes for the intake — Marissa here. Summary for sizing team:

- Token profile: if average prompt is ~80 tokens and average response is ~220 tokens, assume ~300 tokens end-to-end per request. For generative models, include ~10% overhead for tokenization/metadata.
- Concurrency -> GPU mapping: for an MPT-30B/HF-quantized class model on an A100-like pod, estimate ~12–18 interactive concurrent sessions per GPU for sub-400ms p95 if batching is limited by low tail. If you expect sustained batching (many parallel requests waiting), effective concurrency per GPU increases.
- KV cache: with many short retrieval prompts, prefix/KV cache hit is high if documents are reused. If retrieval is unique per request, caching benefit drops — recommend measuring doc reuse rate.
- Burst handling: recommend reserved capacity sized for sustained baseline + a reserved burst pool (10–25% of reserved) and a temporary burst policy using hosted spill (if Lumina is comfortable).

Action items for Lumina to help us finalize:
1) Confirm microburst durations (minutes) vs hour-level smoothing in the CSV.
2) Provide 95th percentile token counts for prompt and response (or the longest example).
3) Indicate if encryption/key custody or VPC/private deployment is required for the pilot (affects deployment mode).

If Lumina can share a short 48h trace we can run a replay on a staging pod and give concrete GPU counts and expected monthly token cost.

—Marissa
